title: Web: composer, home and sessions
summary: The home, composer and session screens are readable. Their comments cite PRD and decision IDs, every GET is parsed with the generated runtime parsers, and loading and failure text is usually explicit. The jobs chart, search palette and greeting show careful accessibility and hydration work. Change cost and defect risk sit in two places. GoalComposer is one 541-line function (527 counted lines, complexity 37) with 13 state hooks, two fetch effects and its submission code inline. Run admission is written separately in goal-composer and session-panel, and both differ from continue-run. Both cast their POST responses instead of parsing them, mint a new Idempotency-Key on every press with no in-flight guard, and report a lost reply as a sign-in problem (the composer) or a plain failure (the session panel), so a double click or a retry after a timeout can admit two paid runs. Elsewhere in the area: failures read as empty or signed-out states (search, the home account section, the composer's option lists); the waiting notifier stops polling for good after a 401 or 403, which a client-side sign-in does not undo, or after a reply its parser rejects; read-only views fetch in client effects data that their dynamic Server Component pages could render; and every client read hand-writes the same effect. Pure logic such as budget steps, input paths, relative time, chart layout and the waiting diff sits inside .tsx files that the repository's node:test runner cannot load. It is tested only through browser suites, or not at all.

scores.why: Strict TypeScript, Prettier and traceable comments hold, but DH-06 is missed on the admission path (five response casts, no duplicate-submit guard), read-only views are Client Components, and one avatar hard-codes a radius against DS-03.
Imports point at the generated client and lib, but shared run view-models (status labels, the default budget, the goal field id) live in or are copied across feature components.
Eight of the ten files have a function over 60 lines: GoalComposer 527 at complexity 37, JobsPlot 252, SessionPanel 194, SearchPalette 189, HomeActivity 165.
Components interleave data loading, derivation, submission and rendering; the riskiest logic (refusal mapping, budget steps, bar layout, waiting diff) is inline rather than in pure functions.
Pages are thin and each feature has one file, but logic the repo's own lib/*.ts pattern would hold stays in client components, out of reach of unit tests.
Hydration-safe reads, a native modal dialog and parallel server reads are sound, but read-only data is fetched client-side, each screen writes its own fetch effect, and the polling loop is fragile.
Comments mostly explain why and cite PRD and decisions (tab order, nothing sent until Run, body draining); one composer comment is stale and one non-obvious pattern lacks its reason.

GET reads use generated parsers and the search kind map is keyed by the generated union, but admission responses are cast, request bodies are untyped against RunRequest, and status maps are keyed by string.

Loading and failure text is usually explicit, but lost admission replies read as sign-in problems or plain failures, failures read as empty or signed out, option-list failures are swallowed, and polling stops silently.
Browser specs cover the main flows with axe checks, but no unit test covers the area's pure logic, and double submits, lost replies, failure states and polling restarts are untested.
Readable and traceable, with change cost concentrated in GoalComposer and in three diverging copies of run admission.

findings.title: Run admission can start duplicate paid runs: no in-flight guard and a new Idempotency-Key on every press

locations.note: new key per press; the comment states that intent
startSession mints its own key per press, so a press can also create a second session
Run is not disabled while a request is in flight
a null reply or any 5xx falls through to 'error'
the 'error' copy tells the user to sign in
same per-press key
disabled only by !ready
the app's own policy: key kept until the outcome is known; null reply and 5xx treated as unknown at 47-51

findings.evidence: Three POSTs set Idempotency-Key to a fresh crypto.randomUUID() inside the click handler (goal-composer.tsx:262 and 292, session-panel.tsx:55; counted by grep in the area's files). Neither Run button tracks a pending request: goal-composer.tsx:593 disables only on an empty draft or no budget, and session-panel.tsx:190 only on !ready. csrfFetch first GETs /api/csrf (apps/web/lib/csrf-fetch.ts), so each press spans two round trips. A null reply or a 5xx ends in outcome 'error', whose copy is 'That could not be checked. Sign in, then try again.' (goal-composer.tsx:647). That includes the BFF's 503 after its 30 s upstream timeout (apps/web/lib/bff.ts:102 and 120). continue-run.tsx does the opposite: it keeps the key until the outcome is known (20-21, 39) and treats a null reply or 5xx as unknown (47-51).
findings.impact: A double click admits a second run, and so does a second press after an admission that the API committed but whose reply was lost or timed out. With an Expert, it also creates a second session. Each run reserves budget and calls models. The user is told to sign in when the real state is unknown. The app also now applies two contradictory idempotency policies to the same endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Adopt continue-run's policy in one shared admission hook: (1) disable Run while a request is in flight; (2) keep the Idempotency-Key, and on the Expert path the created session id, until the outcome is definite; (3) keep the request body fixed while the outcome is unknown, as ContinueRun locks its model choice (continue-run.tsx:94-97), because the API refuses a reused key with different content (application/runs.py:117-118); (4) clear the key only after acceptance or a 4xx refusal; (5) show a null reply or 5xx as 'not known yet, press Run again to check', and keep the sign-in copy for 401 not_signed_in. Share the unknown-outcome rule with the command helper WRUN-03 proposes. Add browser cases that double-click Run and that drop the admission reply, each asserting one run. Write those tests first.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Disable duplicate submits with server idempotency as the correctness mechanism.' The server key stays the correctness mechanism; the client stops minting a new one per press and adds the in-flight guard. No run state or scheduling moves into Next.js.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed the three fresh-key POSTs, the missing in-flight guard and the sign-in copy for an unknown outcome. Added step (3): the admission fingerprint covers the goal, budget, files, Expert and model (application/runs.py:202-217), so a retry that sends an edited draft under the kept key is refused rather than replayed.

findings.title: Admission replies are cast instead of parsed, and request bodies are untyped

locations.note: POST /v1/sessions reply cast to { id: string }; it returns SessionView
202 reply cast to { run_id: string } instead of parseRunAccepted
error body cast instead of parseErrorResponse
RunRequest body built as an untyped literal
same RunAccepted cast
same error-body cast
untyped body; expert_id can be undefined (49-50)
ErrorResponse and parseErrorResponse are generated, as are RunAccepted (8526), RunRequest (8673) and SessionCreate (8801)

findings.evidence: Every GET in these two files is parsed, but the admission POSTs are not. goal-composer.tsx:273 uses `((await reply.json()) as { id: string }).id`. goal-composer.tsx:311 and session-panel.tsx:65 cast to `{ run_id: string }`. Refusals are cast to `{ code?: string; message?: string } | null` (goal-composer.tsx:318-321, session-panel.tsx:68-70). That makes five assertions, the ESLint consistent-type-assertions hits for these files. The three bodies go through JSON.stringify untyped, so session-panel.tsx:60 passes an expert_id typed string | null | undefined; JSON.stringify drops an undefined key, but `satisfies RunRequest` would reject it under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, since RunRequest declares `expert_id?: string | null`. The generated createWorkSession (generated.ts:9482-9483) shows that POST /v1/sessions returns SessionView.
findings.impact: This is the paid admission path. If run_id, id or code is renamed or retyped, the code still compiles and fails quietly: the success link becomes /runs/undefined, and refusals fall to the generic message. The project's ESLint config does not flag these casts, so nothing stops more of them.
findings.recommendation: Parse with the generated functions. Use parseSessionView for the session reply and parseRunAccepted for the 202. Call parseErrorResponse inside a readError(reply) helper that returns null for other bodies, such as an HTML error page; the API itself turns every validation failure into an ErrorResponse with status 422 (api/errors.py:29-32). Treat a ContractError on a 202 as an unknown outcome (the run may exist), not a refusal. Declare the bodies with `satisfies RunRequest` and `satisfies SessionCreate`. Consider publishing the refusal codes as an enum on ErrorResponse in Pydantic and regenerating, so the Outcome union stops mirroring them by hand. Enable @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-assertions for app code, with narrow, documented exceptions.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 and rules/nextjs.md: generated API types plus explicit response parsing at untrusted boundaries, and no blanket type assertions; rules/contracts.md: TypeScript types do not validate JSON. The fix uses existing generated parsers and hand-edits nothing generated; any new enum is added in Pydantic and regenerated.
findings.verifierNote: The five casts match eslint.json, apps/web/eslint.config.mjs enables only the Next presets, and the generated parsers sit at the cited lines. Corrected two details: the API answers every validation failure with an ErrorResponse 422 (api/errors.py:29-32), so a FastAPI HTTPValidationError body never arrives; and an undefined expert_id is dropped by JSON.stringify, so the defect is the untyped body rather than a wrong value on the wire.

findings.title: GoalComposer is a 541-line component with 13 state hooks, three effects and inline submission

findings.evidence: Lines 113-653 hold the whole composer. They contain 13 useState hooks (128-140) and a store read (114); effects for focus (116-127), the option lists (143-166) and the preview (169-194); budget math in render (196-216); file admission (218-245); session start and admission (256-341); and 310 lines of JSX ending in a nine-way nested ternary (607-648). outcome, runId and refusal are separate hooks updated in pairs (277-278, 312-313, 323-324), so the queued branch still has to check runId === null (640). Budget choices come from `for (value = min; value <= max; value += step)` over server values (199-205), and the contract sets no minimum on step_micro_usd.
findings.impact: Every change to a chip, a refusal or the attachments lands in one 37-branch function whose states must be kept consistent by hand. The admission and option-loading defects in this area are hidden inside it. Its pure parts can't be unit-tested where they are, and a zero step from the server would hang the render.
findings.recommendation: Split by responsibility. Give the draft, the option lists, the preview, the attachments and admission their own hooks. Make budget choices and file admission pure, JSX-free functions; budget choices should reject step <= 0 and cap the count. Move the markup into four presentational children. Use useReducer only for admission, where fields must change together; the rest of the state is independent. A form library would add little, because validation is one non-empty check plus the server's refusals. Fix admission first, with its tests, because composer.spec.ts pins the current behavior.

findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 asks for small cohesive modules and keeps UI view models distinct. The reducer models the admission request (idle, submitting, accepted, refused, unknown), not RunStatus, so it adds no second run-state enum; the run's state stays RunAccepted.status.
findings.verifierNote: Counted 13 useState hooks, the store read, three effects and the nine-way outcome chain at the cited lines; run() matches eslint.json (65 lines, complexity 18), and git log shows 14 commits on the file. The zero-step hang is defensive: the API sends a fixed US$0.25 step today (domain/budgets.py:7), though the contract does not forbid zero.

Render that result with one AdmissionMessage component: role=status when accepted, role=alert for refusals, and the settings links in one place. findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: centralize error handling and avoid duplicated business rules. The mapping still comes from the server's codes, so no client rule is invented and admission remains a server decision.
findings.verifierNote: Compared the three mappings side by side: only the composer links to settings, the session panel folds credential_invalid, credential_unavailable and budget refusals into one sentence, and the composer announces a queued run with role=alert.

findings.title: Failures render as signed out, empty results or nothing

locations.note: a null session renders 'Signed out' and 'You are not signed in.'; Sign in link at 90-96
fetchSession returns null when signed out and on any API failure
a refused reply becomes an empty result list
a network failure does too
which then reads 'Nothing in this workspace matches.'
option-list refusals are drained and dropped, and errors are swallowed

findings.evidence: page.tsx branches six times on session === null (42, 59, 71, 75, 79, 90). fetchSession returns null from its catch (lib/service-status.ts:58-59) when the API is unreachable, so a signed-in user with the API down sees 'Signed out', 'You are not signed in.' and a Sign in button. In search, a refused reply yields an empty list through `reply.ok ? parseSearchResults(...).results : []` (search-palette.tsx:75-77), the catch does the same (83-87), and both show 'Nothing in this workspace matches.' (211-212). In the composer, a refused experts or models read is drained and nothing else happens, and `.catch(() => undefined)` (162) swallows network and ContractError failures. The selects then offer only their defaults, with no message.
findings.impact: When the local API is down, the app tells the user to sign in, says nothing matches, or says nothing at all, which sends the user to the wrong fix. These are the states DH-06 asks to keep apart.
findings.recommendation: Return a discriminated result from the session read (signed_out, signed_in or unavailable), and when it is unavailable, show that the account can't be checked instead of offering Sign in. Give search a failed status with its own message. Show one line under the chips when experts or models can't be read, so the user knows the lists are incomplete. The shared resource hook in the fetch-effect finding provides the failed state.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: represent loading, empty, denied, unavailable and retryable states deliberately; rules/nextjs.md: explicit error, empty and loading states. Error details stay on the server, as fetchServiceStatus already keeps them.
findings.verifierNote: fetchSession's catch returns null, so an unreachable API renders 'Signed out' and a Sign in link. The Services section on the same page does show 'Python API: unavailable', which softens the contradiction but does not remove it. The search and option-list paths behave as stated.

findings.title: The waiting notifier stops polling for good after a 401 or a rejected reply

locations.note: a 401 or 403 returns without scheduling the next poll
mounted once in the root layout, so client navigation never remounts it
sign-in is router.push plus router.refresh, not a page load
bad JSON or a ContractError rejects poll(), so line 71 is never reached
timer is undefined while a request is in flight
so restart() during a request starts a second loop
fixed 4 s interval and no backoff while the API is down

findings.evidence: poll() sets timer = undefined (36), awaits the fetch, and reschedules only at its end (71). A 401 or 403 returns first (69). The comment at 68 expects the page to reload and restart it, but sign-in navigates client-side (sign-in-form.tsx:31-32), and the notifier lives in the root layout (layout.tsx:30) with an effect keyed on the stable router, so nothing restarts it. parseRunList(await reply.json()) (47) is outside any try, and poll runs as `void poll()`, so a rejected reply ends the loop with an unhandled rejection. restart() cannot cancel an in-flight poll, because the timer it checks at 75 is undefined then. Toggling the setting off and on within one request therefore leaves two loops. Failures retry every 4 s indefinitely.
findings.impact: With the setting on, notifications silently stop until a reload after the user signs out and back in, or opens the app on an expired session. That disables PRD-Studio SE-05. One reply the parser rejects has the same effect. The forked loop and the missing backoff are rarer and cheaper, but come from the same structure.
findings.recommendation: Make every exit path schedule the next poll: wrap each poll in try/finally, back off after failures (doubling from 4 s up to a cap, reset on success), and either retry slowly after a 401 or 403 (for example every 60 s) or remount the notifier when the signed-in user changes. Add a generation counter that restart() increments, so a stale poll never reschedules. Extract the newly-waiting diff as a pure function with unit tests, and cover the loop with fake timers instead of the fixed five-second waits in tests/browser/settings-sections.spec.ts.
findings.ruleCheck: PRD-Studio SE-05: read only the app's own API and raise one notification per newly waiting run; both stay. The loop only reads, so it schedules no business work in the browser (DH-06).
findings.verifierNote: Traced every exit path: a 401 or 403 returns before line 71, a parser rejection escapes `void poll()`, and restart() cannot clear a poll in flight, so a second loop starts. The effect depends only on the stable router, and sign-in is client-side, so the root-layout notifier is never restarted.

findings.title: Read-only home, data and session views fetch in client effects data their dynamic pages could render

locations.note: no interaction; three client reads in an effect
no interaction; one client read
the session the page could pass in
/api/v1/runs at the default limit of 100 to show five (191)
the page awaits four reads with no Suspense boundary

findings.evidence: HomeActivity and DataSummary have no event handlers. They are Client Components only so they can fetch in an effect, so they render 'Loading.' first and carry their own failure branches. HomeActivity also needs three non-null assertions (79-81). The generated client already has server operations for these reads: getRetentionSummary, getWorkSession and listApprovals (packages/api-client/src/generated.ts:9386, 9486 and 9294). lib/service-status.ts already builds the member clients they need. Recent runs downloads up to 100 runs to show five (68, 191), although the endpoint accepts limit. On the server, page.tsx blocks on four reads before anything streams, and fetchReadiness runs twice per render (page.tsx:36, app-shell.tsx:19).
findings.impact: Each of these views adds a round trip through the BFF and a loading flash for data the server can read with a typed client, and each duplicates effect code. On Home, the slowest read delays the composer, which needs none of them.
findings.recommendation: Make HomeActivity and DataSummary async Server Components. Feed them from server-only helpers beside fetchReadiness: needs-you runs, five recent runs with limit=5 and pending approvals for Home, and the retention summary for the data page. Pass SessionPanel a server-read SessionView so it keeps only the form. Move the home page's own reads into Suspense-wrapped sections so the composer streams first. Wrap fetchReadiness and fetchSession in React cache() so the shell and the page share one read per request. The generated listRuns takes no query parameters, so its helper uses requestJson plus parseRunList until the generator supports them.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: prefer Server Components, use Client Components for actual interaction, and keep workspace data out of shared caches. The reads stay per request (the session cookie makes the pages dynamic, and the reads use no-store) and go through the existing server-only member client.
findings.verifierNote: HomeActivity and DataSummary have no handlers; getRetentionSummary, getWorkSession and listApprovals exist at the cited lines, and /api/v1/runs defaults to RUN_LIST_SIZE = 100 (run_projection.py:55). The second readiness read was inferred from the two call sites, not measured.

findings.title: Every client read writes its own fetch effect, and the copies already disagree

locations.note: option lists
preview
search
job counts
retention
the refused body is never read
says why a refused body must be read
/api/models, which the child RunDisclosure fetches again (run-disclosure.tsx:47)

findings.evidence: Eight effects in this area repeat the same shape: a `let live = true`, `let active = true` or `let stopped = false` flag, a no-store fetch, parse on ok, drain on refusal, then a failed flag. They are at goal-composer.tsx:144 and 170, home-activity.tsx:64, jobs-chart.tsx:86, data-summary.tsx:23, search-palette.tsx:68, session-panel.tsx:25 and waiting-notifier.tsx:28. A grep for those flags finds 29 in 24 files under apps/web components, app and lib. home-activity.tsx:73 says an unread refusal keeps its connection open, yet session-panel.tsx:31-33 never reads the refused body, and every `if (!live) return` exits before reading. The composer and its RunDisclosure child each fetch /api/models on mount.
findings.impact: Each copy decides liveness, body handling, error typing and the failure state again. A fix like the ones in the failure-state finding must be repeated eight times in this area and 29 times across the app, and the copies have already drifted.
findings.recommendation: Add one hook, useApiResource(url, parse). It should abort with an AbortController on cleanup (which also releases the connection), cancel refused bodies, turn a ContractError into the failed state, and return a discriminated state. Use it for the reads that must stay client-side here: the composer's option lists and preview, search, and the jobs chart inside the client OperationsPanel. Pass the models list from GoalComposer to RunDisclosure instead of fetching it twice.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: centralize error handling; rules/nextjs.md: explicit error, empty and loading states. The hook only reads, and the generated parsers remain the validation step.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted 29 liveness flags in 24 files (grep for `let live = true`, `let active = true` and `let stopped = false`); session-panel.tsx:31-33 does not read the refused body, and both the composer and RunDisclosure request /api/models.

findings.evidence: SearchPalette (24-218, 189 counted lines) handles opening the dialog and returning focus (35-47, 103-106), the global shortcut (49-63), the debounced fetch (65-94), arrow wrap-around and Enter (151-163), and the status text (207-213). The shortcut is defined three times: in the key matcher (52-55), in aria-keyshortcuts and the kbd label (115, 121-126), and in the SE-07 registry entry (lib/shortcuts.ts:14-17). `shown` holds the current results whenever the query is non-empty (108), so while 'Searching.' is announced, Enter opens a result for the previous term.
findings.impact: The keyboard behavior is correct today, but none of it can be unit-tested inline. A shortcut change needs three coordinated edits, and typing quickly then pressing Enter opens a stale result.
findings.recommendation: Extract three pieces: a useSearch(query) hook returning { status, term, results }, with a failed status (see the failure-state finding); a pure moveActive(current, key, count) in lib/keyboard.ts; and a useShortcut(match, handler) hook shared with NewRun's ⇧⌘O. Give each SHORTCUTS entry its matcher and aria-keyshortcuts value. Let Enter act only when the results belong to the current term, and ignore keys during IME composition.

<SearchResults search={search} active={active} />  <SearchStatus search={search} />

findings.ruleCheck: Decision 0022 D3 (⌘K opens search, and no shortcut acts in a text field) and PRD-Studio SE-07 (every shortcut in one list) stay true; the registry becomes the single source instead of a manual copy.
